random_rejection.what: The floor every real method must beat: random angle, random position, keep the try that does not hit anything.
random_rejection.how: Each part gets up to 300 random poses inside a cube; a pose is rejected if its box comes within the clearance of a placed box. When stuck the cube grows 10%. Three restarts, best kept.

shelf_packing.what: Rows and layers, like filling a bookshelf.
shelf_packing.how: Lay every part flat (shortest side up), tallest first. Fill a row along x, then the next row in y, then a new layer in z when the square floor is full.
strengths: Predictable layers; good for flat parts.
weaknesses: A tall part sets the whole layer height.
Space above shorter parts is wasted.

box_bottom_left.how: Largest box first. Candidate corners are every combination of placed-box edges on a square floor; take the lowest, then frontmost, then leftmost free corner over the 6 orientations.
weaknesses: Fixed floor size limits the layout.
Boxes only: cannot use a concave part's notch.

box_extreme_points.what: Bottom-left with far fewer candidates and a better objective.
box_extreme_points.how: Only the three corners each placed box exposes (+x, +y, +z) are candidates. Choose the corner and orientation that keep the overall bounding box smallest.
strengths: Densest plain box method on cuboids.
weaknesses: The greedy volume objective builds slabs (aspect 4 to 6).

empty_maximal_spaces.what: Keeps an explicit list of the empty space as maximal boxes.
empty_maximal_spaces.how: Start with one big empty box. Each part goes at the min corner of the empty box (and orientation) that keeps the overall box smallest; every empty box it cuts is split into up to six boxes around it, and boxes inside others are dropped.
strengths: Best constructive box method on most categories.
Fast (0.1 s); container mode is natural.
weaknesses: Greedy: one bad early choice is never revisited.

force_based.what: Physics-style: throw the boxes in, squeeze, push overlaps apart.
force_based.how: Every box starts at a random spot, overlapping. Repeat 40 times: squeeze all boxes 10% toward the centroid, then push overlapping pairs apart along their shallowest overlap. Keep the tightest overlap-free state. Three restarts.
strengths: No placement order; all parts move at once.
Constraints can be added as extra forces.
weaknesses: Barely above random on concave parts.

force_based_v2.what: force_based with an anisotropic squeeze, compaction and re-orientation.
force_based_v2.how: Axes wider than a target cube are pulled in harder; after each pass every box slides toward the origin along z, y, x as far as the others allow and re-picks the orientation that overlaps least.
strengths: 10 to 25% denser than v1, rows gone.
weaknesses: Still boxes, still below the greedy methods.

voxel_bottom_left.what: Bottom-left on the real shape, voxelized.
voxel_bottom_left.how: Each part is voxelized at 2 mm, grown by half the clearance. For each orientation an FFT convolution of the grid with the part gives the overlap count at every position at once; keep the free position that keeps the box smallest.
strengths: Best constructive method on real shapes.
weaknesses: The 2 mm grid and the clearance eat most of the interlock gain.

heightfield_drop.what: Huai-Yi's method rebuilt on the benchmark grid: drop parts onto a height map.
heightfield_drop.how: The stack is a 2D height map; each part has a bottom and a top profile per column. Drop at every (x, y) and orientation: landing height = max over its columns of (stack top minus part bottom). Keep the landing that keeps the box smallest.
strengths: No 3D search: 5x faster than voxel, within 0.02 of it.
weaknesses: A column is solid from bottom to top, so nothing slides under an overhang.

best_of_fast.what: Run the six constructive packers and keep the densest.
best_of_fast.how: Shelf, bottom-left, extreme points, EMS, voxel and heightfield on the same parts; keep the result with the most parts placed, then the highest density.
strengths: Never worse than its best member.
weaknesses: Cost is the sum of six.

simulated_annealing.what: Search over the placement order and orientations, decoded by the voxel packer.
simulated_annealing.how: Start from largest-first. Each step swaps two parts or re-orients one, decodes with the voxel packer (orientations fixed), accepts if density rises or with probability exp(gain / T); T falls from 0.05 to 0.001 over a 5 s budget.
strengths: Most compact boxes and lowest COM offset of any method.
weaknesses: 5 s per packing; result depends on budget and CPU.
About 100 decodes is a small search for 10! orders.

genetic_algorithm.what: A population of (order, orientations) genomes bred for density, decoded by the voxel packer.
genetic_algorithm.how: Population 12; each generation keeps the best 6 and breeds 6 children by order crossover (a slice of parent 1 stays, parent 2 fills the rest in its order), orientations from either parent, one mutation. 5 s budget.
strengths: Best density on most categories at k = 10.

genetic_heightfield.what: The genetic search with the heightfield drop as decoder.
genetic_heightfield.how: Same genome and operators; each decode is about 10x cheaper than voxel, so the same 5 s evaluates about 10x more orders and orientations.
strengths: Usually the best search method at k = 20 and 30.

genetic_box.what: The genetic search with the exact extreme-points box decoder.
genetic_box.how: Same genome and operators; decodes are about 50x cheaper and have no grid rounding. Boxes only.
strengths: Shows how much the voxel grid costs on box-like parts.
weaknesses: Diagnostic more than a contender on concave parts.

skyline_3d.what: Skyline packing: the stack is a height map of box tops.
skyline_3d.how: A square floor carries a 1 mm height map. Each part's box, in each orientation, is tried at the 2D corners of placed boxes and rests on the highest point under it; keep the lowest resulting top, then the least wasted volume. Four floor sizes tried, densest kept.
weaknesses: Weak on this benchmark: waste under boxes adds up.

wall_building.what: Container-loading classic: fill vertical walls one after another.
wall_building.how: The first part of a wall sets its depth. The wall's face is filled with 2D maximal empty rectangles by any remaining part whose box depth fits in some orientation; when nothing fits, a new wall starts behind it.
strengths: Natural for container mode and layered assemblies.
weaknesses: Wall depth is set by one part, so depth is wasted.

dblf_24.what: Deep-bottom-left-fill on voxels with all 24 orientations.
dblf_24.how: Like voxel bottom-left, but every axis-aligned orientation is tried (not only the 6 distinct box shapes) and the position is the deepest, then lowest, then leftmost free cell inside a fixed floor.
strengths: More orientations than any other grid method.
weaknesses: About 4x the cost of voxel bottom-left.
The fixed floor can force a tall stack.

beam_search.what: Deterministic tree search over placement sequences with a beam.
beam_search.how: Each level places one more part: every partial packing in the beam is extended by every remaining part in every orientation (extreme-points decoder), scored by the density reachable if the rest fit perfectly, and the best 8 are kept. 5 s cap, then greedy.
strengths: Cheaper than the genetic methods on small k.

grasp_ems.what: GRASP: many randomized EMS constructions, keep the best.
grasp_ems.how: For 5 s: perturb the largest-first order with neighbour swaps, run EMS picking each part's spot at random among the 3 best choices, keep the densest valid construction.
strengths: Best box-based density in the smoke tests (0.82 on cuboids).
